cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: A transaction groups reads and writes into one unit that commits fully or not at all, with ACID guarantees: atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Isolation levels trade correctness for concurrency: Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable. PostgreSQL uses MVCC so readers do not block writers. For read-modify-write like inventory, use an atomic UPDATE, SELECT FOR UPDATE (pessimistic) or a version check (optimistic, retry on conflict).

questions.q: Is an inventory update in a transaction safe by default?
questions.a: No. Under Read Committed two transactions can both read 10, both write 9, and one update is lost.

questions.q: What does Read Committed prevent and allow?
questions.a: Prevents dirty reads; still allows non-repeatable reads and phantoms.
Pessimistic locks before reading. Optimistic reads without a lock and checks a version on write, retrying on conflict.
